meta.title: MiniGAN: A Small Generative Adversarial Network for Digit Image Synthesis

questions.text: How can we synthesize 28x28 grayscale digit images using a compact GAN?
questions.goal: To develop a minimal GAN architecture for digit image synthesis.
questions.source_text: We present MiniGAN, a compact generative adversarial network that synthesizes 28x28 grayscale digit images from random noise.

questions.text: What is the architecture of the generator in MiniGAN?
questions.goal: To define the structure and function of the generator.
questions.source_text: The generator maps a latent noise vector to a 28x28 grayscale image.

questions.text: What is the architecture of the discriminator in MiniGAN?
questions.goal: To define the structure and function of the discriminator.
questions.source_text: The discriminator maps a 28x28 image to a real/fake probability.

questions.text: What dataset is used for training MiniGAN?
questions.goal: To identify the dataset and its characteristics.
questions.source_text: The model is trained on a standard 10-class handwritten-digit dataset of 28x28 grayscale images.

questions.text: What is the training procedure for MiniGAN?
questions.goal: To outline the steps and components involved in training.
To describe the evaluation metrics and methods used.
questions.source_text: We report the generator and discriminator loss curves over training.
